summary: Load-induced 5xx sawtooth from connection multiplexing and accept-queue throttling
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC we observed a persistent, sawtooth pattern of elevated 5xx responses (~4-8% error rate) impacting a single dedicated tenant (AtlasSearch). Errors surfaced at the API gateway as 502/503 and traced to upstream serving runtimes that intermittently closed connections. Impact: downstream API errors and increased latencies for customer traffic; visible customer complaints about failed requests during a large concurrent query window. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool for AtlasSearch.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway error rate jumped around 02:40 UTC coincident with a traffic burst from the customer's ingestion process.
- Accept-queue length on the API gateway frontends spiked from median 7 -> 400+ and oscillated, matching the sawtooth pattern in 5xx.
- Runtime pods reported high socket accept latency and brief threadpool starvation, then recovered, repeating in waves.

Why this ticket: customer-facing impact during sustained burst; requires intervention and root-cause follow-up to avoid recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a dedicated tenant with a large concurrent client using HTTP/2 multiplexing and aggressive connection reuse (simulated customer workload).
2) Start a ramped load test to 10k concurrent streams with many short requests (50-200 tokens).
3) Observe api-gateway accept_queue and 502/503 rates; watch serving-runtime threadpool metrics and accept latency.
4) Note sawtooth error pattern as accept_queue grows, then a partial recovery when upstream backoff triggers, followed by another spike as traffic continues.
comments: 2026-03-10T03:02:00Z - Support (Aisha): Received initial alert from monitoring and customer Slack. Opening ticket and gathering metrics. Assigned to SRE for triage.

2026-03-10T03:12:45Z - SRE (Diego): Correlated 5xx spikes with inbound accept_queue growth; reproduced locally with small load harness. Hypothesis: connection multiplexing + insufficient accept backlog causes accept latency and runtime thread starvation leading to upstream closes.
2026-03-10T03:45:20Z - Customer (AtlasSearch): We saw a spike during our nightly bulk query job — can throttle if needed but need recommendation to avoid impacting users.

2026-03-10T04:05:10Z - SRE (Diego): Pushed temporary kernel tunables to a canary (net.core.somaxconn=1024, net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048) and applied API gateway config to limit concurrent streams per connection. Error rate dropped from ~6% -> ~1.2% on canary within 8 minutes.
2026-03-10T05:20:00Z - Support (Aisha): Customer accepted temporary throttle; scheduling full rollout and postmortem; updating SLA.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses considered: (A) upstream runtime OOM or GPU saturation — ruled out by stable GPU utilization and lack of OOM logs; (B) keystore/TLS churn — TLS metrics showed no renegotiation spike; (C) accept-queue saturation combined with connection multiplexing causing large numbers of short-lived requests to pile on accept path — supported by accept_queue and kernel drop counters. Evidence: canary changes to somaxconn and limiting concurrent streams reduced error rate. Additional observation: runtimes exhibited ephemeral threadpool stalls when accept latency > 80ms. Linked to earlier ticket SUP-472901 which showed similar accept-queue behavior during tenant shifts.
resolution: Applied a multi-step remediation: 1) Immediate: rolled kernel parameter updates (net.core.somaxconn and tcp_max_syn_backlog) across AtlasSearch dedicated host pool via automation and applied per-route connection concurrency limit at API gateway (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-gateway/pull/3987). 2) Medium-term: deployed runtime patch reducing accept spin and increasing worker handoff threshold (runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021) to avoid threadpool starvation. 3) Customer-facing workaround: advised AtlasSearch to throttle ingestion concurrency and switch to larger batched requests where possible for the next 48 hours. Outcome: error rate returned to baseline (~0.5%) within 12 minutes of the full rollout.
follow_up_actions: Create monitoring alert when api_gateway.accept_queue_len > 200 for > 2 minutes (owner: SRE).
Add a soft-shed policy to ingress-prioritizer to start shedding non-critical short requests when accept_queue > 300 (owner: Runtime team).
Document recommended tenant-side client settings for high-concurrency workloads in Customer KB and include suggested batching/connection limits (owner: Developer Experience).
Run a postmortem and include capacity playbook updates; schedule retro with AtlasSearch to review ingestion patterns (owner: Support + Customer Success).
